payload.viable_set: Two viable candidates on the front: K1 poll-in-board and K2 poll-dedicated - both genuinely build the lane; K1 dominates on unattended-safety with parity elsewhere, K2 is the recorded alternative for the independent-scale world. Not a manufactured pair - they differ on the one real axis (process topology) the DSM left candidate-variable.
payload.complete_allocation: Both allocate all nine functions along the shared OUTBOUND/INBOUND/CREDENTIAL clusters: K1 puts OUTBOUND (G1,G2,G3,G8) and INBOUND (G4,G5,G6,G7) in one phone module whose poll loop the board process drives, CREDENTIAL (G1 config read, G9 protect) in a config loader both use; K2 identical except INBOUND runs in a dedicated watcher process. Interfaces = cluster edges: OUTBOUND<->transport {topic, brief, actions, id}; INBOUND<->transport {topic, cursor}; INBOUND<->Gate {hash, channel}; CREDENTIAL feeds both {topic, token}. Rationale per candidate in the chart evidence.
payload.criteria_traced: C1-C5 each carry their requirement ids and weights (30/25/20/15/10), derived from the register and the stakeholder tensions at derive_criteria; the channel choice explicitly excluded as owner-ruled, not a criterion.
payload.front_recorded: Front {K1, K2}; K3 push-subscribe eliminated (unattended surface for a moot latency win); K2 kept-not-selected with its scale trigger. All eliminations reasoned.
payload.feasibility_checked: K1: every mechanism exists - the board process already long-lives and polls, Gate.bless already records channel, fetch is present, seDir holds the config; feasible by construction, the one unknown (does an in-board poll loop stay within the 1s law and not wedge the board) is the M6 spike. K2: feasible too but adds a supervised process; its feasibility cost IS its C2 deduction, verified against the existing se_ps supervision surface.
